title: Ratios, Rates, Proportional Relationships, and Units
subtitle: Master dimensional analysis, proportions, density, work-rate, and mixture problems

sections.title: The Master Technique: Dimensional Analysis
sections.content:
Every unit conversion, rate problem, and density question uses the same master technique: **dimensional analysis** (also called the factor-label method).

The idea: multiply by fractions equal to 1 (where numerator and denominator are the same quantity in different units) to **cancel unwanted units**.

$$42 \frac{\text{posters}}{\text{min}} \times 60 \frac{\text{min}}{\text{hour}} = 2520 \frac{\text{posters}}{\text{hour}}$$

The units cancel just like variables in algebra. Practice: always write out units explicitly.

sections.title: Cancel Units Like Fractions
sections.content:
Write the starting rate as a fraction. Multiply by conversion fractions until you reach the target unit.

**Rule:** Place the unit you want to eliminate in the **denominator** of your conversion fraction.

**Speed conversions to remember:**
- Seconds → hours: multiply by 3,600 (60 × 60)
- Minutes → hours: multiply by 60
- Hours → minutes: multiply by 1/60

sections.title: Example: Speed Conversion
sections.problem: The International Space Station orbits at 4.76 miles per second. What is its speed in miles per hour?

steps.description: Convert seconds to hours: multiply by (60 sec/min) and (60 min/hr)

sections.tip: Shortcut: multiply any per-second rate by 3,600 to get per-hour. Multiply any per-minute rate by 60 to get per-hour.

sections.title: Example: Multi-Step Unit Conversion
sections.problem: How many fluid ounces are equivalent to 76 quarts? (Given: 8 fl oz = 1 cup; 4 cups = 1 quart)

steps.description: Set up the full conversion chain
steps.math: 76 \text{ qt} \times \frac{4 \text{ cups}}{1 \text{ qt}} \times \frac{8 \text{ fl oz}}{1 \text{ cup}}

sections.title: Two Equal Ratios — Cross-Multiply or Scale
sections.content:
A proportion sets two ratios equal: $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}$

**Cross-multiply:** $ad = bc$

**Or scale up/down:** find what factor connects the two ratios, then apply it.

**Example:** $\dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{x}{15}$. Since $5 \times 3 = 15$, multiply the numerator too: $x = 3 \times 3 = 9$.

sections.title: Example: Find a Missing Value
sections.problem: The ratio $140 : m$ is equivalent to $4 : 28$. Find $m$.
sections.tip: Always simplify the ratio first. 4:28 simplifies to 1:7, making the proportion much easier.

sections.title: Example: Maps and Scale Factors
sections.problem: On a map, 1 inch represents 25 miles. Two cities are $3.5$ inches apart on the map. What is the actual distance between them?

sections.title: Density = Mass ÷ Volume
sections.content:
$$\text{Density} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}} \qquad \text{Mass} = \text{Density} \times \text{Volume} \qquad \text{Volume} = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}}$$

**Population density** works the same way:
$$\text{Population} = \text{Density} \times \text{Area}$$

**Strategy:** write the formula, identify what's given, solve for the unknown.

sections.title: Example: Population Density
sections.problem: Iceland's population density increased from 2.5 people/km² to 3.3 people/km². The land area is 100,250 km². By how many people did the population increase?

steps.description: Population = density × area. Find both populations

sections.tip: Shortcut: change in population = change in density × area = (3.3 − 2.5) × 100,250 = 0.8 × 100,250 = 80,200.

sections.title: Combined Work: Add the Rates
sections.content:
Work-rate problems ask how long it takes multiple workers (or machines) working together to complete a job.

**Key formula:** when workers combine, **add their individual rates**.

$$\text{Combined rate} = \text{Rate}_1 + \text{Rate}_2$$

**Individual rate** = fraction of job completed per unit time.
- If worker A completes the job in 4 hours: rate = $\dfrac{1}{4}$ job/hour
- If worker B completes the job in 6 hours: rate = $\dfrac{1}{6}$ job/hour
- Together: rate = $\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{5}{12}$ job/hour
- Time together = $\dfrac{1}{\text{combined rate}} = \dfrac{12}{5} = 2.4$ hours

sections.title: Example: Two Workers Together
sections.problem: Pump A can fill a tank in 3 hours. Pump B can fill the same tank in 5 hours. Working together, how long will they take?

steps.description: Rate A = 1/3 tank/hr. Rate B = 1/5 tank/hr. Combined rate:

sections.tip: Always faster than either alone, but not as fast as the sum. The combined time is between 0 and the faster individual time.

sections.title: Example: Find One Rate When Combined Rate is Known
sections.problem: Two machines together produce 180 parts per hour. Machine A produces 120 parts per hour on its own. How many parts per hour does Machine B produce?

steps.description: Combined = Rate A + Rate B → solve for Rate B

sections.answer: Machine B produces $60$ parts per hour

sections.title: Example: Solve an Algebraic Proportion
sections.problem: If $\dfrac{x}{y} = 4$ and $\dfrac{24x}{ny} = 4$, what is the value of $n$?
sections.tip: When two variables appear in a proportion, substitute one in terms of the other to get a single equation.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: **Dimensional analysis:** write units and cancel them like fractions — don't guess, cancel
**Proportions:** cross-multiply, or find the scale factor and apply it directly
**Density:** Mass = Density × Volume; Population = Density × Area
**Work rates:** rate = 1/time; combined rate = sum of individual rates; time = 1/combined rate
**Algebraic proportions:** substitute one variable in terms of the other

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Unit conversions: inverting the conversion fraction (putting the wrong unit in the numerator)
- Cross-multiplying: writing ad = bc correctly, but then dividing by the wrong term
- Work-rate: adding times instead of rates (you add rates, not times)
- Density: confusing which formula to use — write D = M/V, then solve for what's unknown
- Scale factors: multiplying when you should divide (use dimensional analysis to check)

sat_tips: Always write units — units that should cancel will cancel automatically if you set up the fraction correctly
For work-rate problems: individual rate = 1 / (time to complete alone). Combined = sum of rates
Map/model problems are just proportions: set up real/scale = real/scale and cross-multiply
Density shortcut: change in total = change in rate × constant (e.g., population increase = density increase × fixed area)
